actionable_insights: Aim for about 10% weight loss under medical guidance.
Eliminate sugary drinks and added sugars.

disease_sections.title: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
disease_sections.overview: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the term for a range of conditions caused by a build-up of fat in the liver. It's usually seen in people who are overweight or obese.

current_status.interpretation: Your findings suggest early fatty liver changes with an increased risk of progression. Lifestyle improvements and regular monitoring are recommended.
current_status.clinical_warning: Timely medical review is recommended for ongoing liver monitoring.

contributing_factors: Mildly low total protein and globulin

tips: Aim for about 10% weight loss under medical guidance.
Eliminate sugary drinks and added sugars.
exercise: Aim for up to 300 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly.

recommendations: Monitor liver enzymes, FIB-4, and FibroScan.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: With consistent care, your liver health can still improve.

disease_sections.title: Metabolic Syndrome
disease_sections.overview: Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of conditions including increased waist circumference, high blood sugar, elevated blood pressure, abnormal cholesterol, and high triglycerides.

current_status.interpretation: Your score is still healthy but nearing the upper end of this range. Improving lifestyle quality now can reduce future metabolic risk.
current_status.clinical_warning: Persistent or worsening metabolic abnormalities should be medically reviewed even without symptoms.

tips: Exercise regularly at a comfortable intensity.

recommendations: Choose a vegetable-rich, minimally processed diet.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Focused lifestyle improvements can still meaningfully reduce your overall metabolic risk.

disease_sections.title: Hypertension
disease_sections.overview: Hypertension, also known as high or raised blood pressure, is a condition in which the blood vessels have persistently raised pressure.

current_status.interpretation: Your blood-pressure risk is in an increased range. Consistent lifestyle changes and regular monitoring can help improve this score.
current_status.clinical_warning: Timely healthcare follow-up is appropriate if home readings remain elevated or are rising. Urgent assessment is needed when severe symptoms occur with a very high reading.

tips: Make lower-sodium meals, regular exercise, and weight management central weekly goals.
Combine aerobic activity with resistance training on at least two days each week.
Favor steady weight reduction if excess weight is contributing to risk.
exercise: Combine regular aerobic exercise with twice-weekly resistance training.
Work toward 150–300 minutes of moderate activity weekly as tolerated.
Add mobility and stretching to support adherence and comfort.

recommendations: Make sodium awareness part of every meal, including packaged staples and restaurant foods.
Emphasize fibre-rich vegetables, fruit, legumes, and whole grains.
Choose fish, poultry, beans, and lentils instead of cured meats.
Check blood pressure regularly at home if recommended and share the trend with your healthcare professional.
Follow a risk-based schedule for kidney function, glucose, cholesterol, and weight assessment.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Active monitoring plus consistent lifestyle changes can help you regain better control of modifiable risk factors.

disease_sections.title: Obesity
disease_sections.overview: Obesity means your body has more fat than it should, which can put pressure on your heart, joints, and organs, increasing the risk of diabetes, heart disease, and mobility issues.

current_status.interpretation: Your obesity-related score remains in a healthy range. Maintaining current habits can help preserve this result.
current_status.clinical_warning: Consult your healthcare provider if metabolic markers are abnormal or weight loss remains difficult.

tips: Reduce sugary drinks and processed snacks.
exercise: Aim for 150–300 minutes of aerobic activity weekly.
Strength train at least twice weekly.

recommendations: Base meals on vegetables, legumes, whole grains, and lean protein.
Monitor blood pressure, HbA1c, and cholesterol.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: A sustainable lifestyle plan can improve multiple metabolic risk factors.

disease_sections.title: Dyslipidemia
disease_sections.overview: Dyslipidemia refers to abnormal levels of lipids in the bloodstream, which poses a significant risk factor for cardiovascular (CV) diseases.

current_status.interpretation: Your cholesterol or triglycerides are noticeably above the healthy range. This increased-risk stage calls for consistent lifestyle changes and regular monitoring to reduce future cardiovascular risk.
current_status.clinical_warning: Consult your doctor for regular monitoring. This is a preventive step, not an emergency.

tips: Aim for 7-10% weight loss if overweight.
Exercise regularly with cardio and strength training.

recommendations: Choose fish, legumes, and lean proteins.
Repeat lipid profile and blood sugar in about 6 months.
Monitor weight, waist, and blood pressure.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Healthy lifestyle changes can significantly improve your cholesterol levels.

disease_sections.title: Type 2 Diabetes
disease_sections.overview: Type 2 diabetes is a condition where the body doesn't use insulin properly, leading to high blood sugar levels. You are more likely to develop type 2 diabetes if you have risk factors, such as overweight or obesity, and a family history of the disease.

current_status.interpretation: Your type 2 diabetes-related score remains in a healthy range. Maintaining current habits can help preserve this result.
current_status.clinical_warning: Consult your doctor for monitoring and lifestyle guidance.

tips: Aim for about 7% weight loss if overweight.
Avoid sugary drinks and refined carbohydrates.

recommendations: Prioritise vegetables, legumes, whole grains, and healthy fats.
Repeat HbA1c and fasting glucose in about 6 months.
Monitor weight, blood pressure, lipids, and kidney health.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Blood sugar often improves significantly with sustained healthy habits.

disease_sections.title: Thyroid Health
disease_sections.overview: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located in the front of the neck. It produces hormones that play a key role in regulating blood pressure, body temperature, heart rate, metabolism and the reaction of the body to other hormones.

current_status.interpretation: Your thyroid-related score is in a healthy range. Maintaining current habits can help preserve this result.
current_status.clinical_warning: Persistent symptoms or unexplained weight changes should be reviewed by a healthcare professional.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Early lifestyle improvements can help keep your thyroid health on track.

disease_sections.title: Oxidative Stress
disease_sections.overview: Oxidative stress is an imbalance in your body where there are too many unstable molecules called free radicals and not enough antioxidants to neutralize them. This imbalance can damage cells and tissues, potentially contributing to various health problems.

current_status.interpretation: Your oxidative stress score is in an increased-risk range. Strengthening antioxidant-supporting habits and addressing nutrient gaps can help improve this score.
current_status.clinical_warning: Consult your doctor if metabolic markers become abnormal or symptoms persist.

exercise: Aim for 150–300 minutes of aerobic activity weekly.

recommendations: Use healthy fats from nuts and fish.
Monitor blood pressure, glucose, and lipids.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: You remain in a healthy range, and reinforcing healthy habits now provides lasting benefits.

disease_sections.title: Cardiac Health
disease_sections.overview: Cardiac health, also known as cardiovascular health, refers to the overall well-being and proper functioning of the heart and blood vessels. It encompasses the circulatory system's ability to efficiently pump blood, delivering oxygen and nutrients throughout the body.

current_status.interpretation: Your results suggest an increased cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle improvements and regular monitoring can help protect heart and vessel health.
current_status.clinical_warning: Seek medical advice if you develop chest pain or unexplained breathlessness.

exercise: Exercise for at least 150 minutes each week.

recommendations: Follow a Mediterranean or DASH-style diet.
Check blood pressure and cholesterol routinely.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Your heart is in great shape, keep up your healthy lifestyle.
